Subject: Onramp readiness & acceptance protocol (NovaMed pilot MAP)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the time today. As promised, attached is a first-pass on an "onramp" MAP specifically focused on acceptance tests, exit gates, and the go/no-go timeline for the 8-week pilot. High-level ask: please review the acceptance criteria and confirm who will be the sign-off stakeholders on your side so we can lock milestone dates.

Key pieces in the spreadsheet (pilot_onramp_MAP_v1.xlsx):
- Week-by-week milestones and owner (Redwood vs. NovaMed)
- Clear pass/fail acceptance tests for latency, throughput, and PHI-safe handling
- Sign-off matrix and procurement checkpoints (SOW, PO, contract terms)

Proposed acceptance gating (short):
1) Security clearance: SOC2 summary & HIPAA posture reviewed (trial access starts only after procurement handshake)
2) Functional acceptance: 3 canonical prompt families pass precision/recall thresholds on a held-out set
3) Performance acceptance: p95 inference latency under 350ms for sample load profile
4) Operational acceptance: canaries and KV-cache warms work end-to-end in your VPC setup

Next steps / asks for NovaMed:
- Confirm clinical sign-off and procurement contact (I have Emily + procurement email noted but need final names)
- Review the acceptance tests sheet and add any clinical scenarios we should include
- Two available slots this week for a 30-min walkthrough: Thu 6/30 2pm PT or Fri 7/1 11am PT

Attached: pilot_onramp_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — happy to iterate quickly.

— Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear map. A few clarifications from our side before we annotate the sheet: 

1) Data & compliance: we need to confirm that PHI is never persisted outside our VPC and that the pilot can run with our KMS. Can you provide a short SOC2 summary and a statement on data residency for pilot data?

2) Clinical acceptance tests: the clinical team wants the ability to run edge-case transcripts (speech->text->LLM) through the model. Do you support an automated pipeline for ingesting these test transcripts?

3) Latency SLA: 350ms p95 is interesting — we need to understand expected behavior under concurrent load (simulating 10 concurrent clinicians). Is that p95 single-request or per-user?

4) Timing & procurement: procurement asked whether we can start a narrow technical trial before the PO is finalized (proof-of-function only). Procurement included this thread so they can weigh in.

Can we take Fri 7/1 11am PT to walk through the acceptance tests? If not, Thu 2pm works.

Onward —
Emily Sanders
Clinical Product Lead, NovaMed Health
emily.sanders@novamed.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onramp readiness & acceptance protocol (NovaMed pilot MAP)

Emily — thanks, great questions. Answers below and I attached a short doc with the acceptance test checklist.

1) Data & compliance
- Short answer: pilot can run entirely inside your VPC with customer-managed KMS; no customer data is persisted on Redwood-hosted indexes unless you opt in. See attached SOC2-summary.pdf for controls overview.

2) Clinical acceptance automation
- We support an ingest pipeline for batch test transcripts (CSV/JSON). Rishi will own a short runbook to validate the pipeline and run three edge-case batches. We will capture outputs and a regression metric for each prompt family.

3) Latency SLA definition
- The 350ms p95 number is measured under the sample load profile in the spreadsheet (10 concurrent short prompts, 128-token typical reply). For clarity we propose: p95 single-request latency <= 350ms; during simulated 10-concurrent load p95 <= 550ms. If either threshold is missed more than twice during acceptance window, the test is considered failed.

4) Procurement & scope of proof-of-function
- We can do a narrow technical proof-of-function (no PHI, synthetic/obfuscated transcripts) before PO; it requires a short one-page MSA addendum and a signed NDA. Procurement — if you can share the preferred next step (NDA or PO), we can adapt.

Acceptance tests (summary) — see attached acceptance_tests_v1.md and the MAP spreadsheet:
- Functional: pass rate >= 85% on the 3 core prompt families (clinical triage, discharge summary extraction, coding hints)
- Safety: no PHI exfiltration in generated outputs per our redaction checks
- Performance: p95 latency thresholds as above
- Reliability: zero failed inference jobs during 2 test windows (2 separate days)
- Ops: automated canary run and log export to your SIEM within 1 hour of test end

Proposed go/no-go timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP and sign NDA/addendum for proof-of-function
- Week 1: deploy in your VPC, run initial canary, fix any connectivity issues
- Week 2: run acceptance test window #1 (functional + performance)
- Week 3: remediation window if needed; run acceptance test window #2
- Week 4: final sign-off meeting and procurement PO/contract completion

If that works I will: update the MAP spreadsheet with the explicit test windows and owner columns, send the NDA template, and schedule Fri 7/1 11am PT for the walkthrough.

Attached: acceptance_tests_v1.md (checklist), SOC2-summary.pdf (controls overview)

— Ben
